sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Overseas Direct-Operated Hotpot Dining and Condiment Supply

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France-Hong Kong Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (1995)
France-Germany Double Taxation Agreement (1959, as amended 2017)
France-Singapore IGA on Double Taxation (1975, as updated)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: French Monetary and Financial Code, Articles L561-1 et seq. (AML/CFT) and Articles L561-45 through L561-57 (UBO register); Decree No. 2018-1055 of 29 November 2018; Decree No. 2019-1062; EU Directive (EU) 2018/843 (5th AML Directive); EU Regulation 2015/847 (payment transfer transparency); Law No. 2016-1691 (Sapin II) and AFA (French Anti-Corruption Agency) guidelines; sanctions and asset freezing orders under EU regulations and UN resolutions.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport or national identity card of each beneficial owner and signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National authority of the document holder's country (or competent consulate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (for signatory states) or French Consular Legalization (for non-Hague states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (extrait K-bis or equivalent corporate extract) for corporate shareholders
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) or applicable home-country company registry

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney granted to the incorporation agent or representative
Criminal record certificate (extrait de casier judiciaire) or equivalent certificate of no bankruptcy/disqualification
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: French Ministry of Justice (Infogreffe) or equivalent competent authority in the holder's country of residence

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and commercial partners against the EU consolidated list, UN Security Council consolidated list, French FTO lists, OFAC lists (where US nexus exists), and PEP databases verified for foreign PEPs. Enhanced due diligence required under Article L561-10 of the Monetary and Financial Code whenever an external PEP is identified; prior written validation by the compliance officer is mandatory.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Formalités des Entreprises (Guichet Unique): https://formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr, supported by INPI (https://www.inpi.fr) and the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés via Infogreffe (https://www.infogreffe.fr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: French law permits a corporate name (dénomination sociale) in a foreign language provided it uses the Latin script; any non-Latin name must be transliterated into Latin characters and a French transliteration is used for publication in the legal gazette and RCS registration. The name must not be misleading, contrary to public policy, or conflict with existing protected names/trademarks.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon written rejection by the Guichet Unique/RCS, the applicant may (i) request a formal written reason from the RCS; (ii) file an administrative appeal before the President of the Tribunal Judiciaire (commercial chamber) of the registered office location within 15 days of receipt; or (iii) resubmit a revised name after eliminating the conflicting negative certificate/trademark. Legal representation is strongly advised for multijurisdictional filings.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible under the regime of 'domiciliation' (Article R123-208) through an approved domiciliation company, provided the company holds a contractual mail-collection service and the address is in France. For a full-service hotpot restaurant, the operating license and hygiene registration require a physical kitchen and service premises, so a virtual office may only serve as the administrative registered seat and cannot replace the mandatory on-site establishment.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High: estimated 60% probability of unannounced physical inspection in the first 12 months due to mandatory food hygiene (DDPP), fire safety (SDIS), labor inspection (DREETS), and customs controls; statistically above 50% for full-service dining under the national food safety plan (PSN 2023-2025).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal due diligence and UBO structure advisory (lawyer fees for applying UBO piercing rules and drafting structure memo)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed fee under prevailing French bar association benchmarks

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance and trademark pre-search (INPI online registry query plus attorney review)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Law firm / INPI (INPI search itself is no-fee; attorney analysis is fee-based)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for corporate search and conflict opinion

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and consular legalization bundle for up to 4 original UBO/director documents (official procedure fees)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Court of Appeal / Ministry of Foreign Affairs / relevant consulate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff and consular fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Official company registration formalities (Guichet Unique, INPI, RCS / Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce)
Registered office domiciliation (annual fee for approved domiciliation company)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Commercial market rate for approved domiciliation provider

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of legal announcement (annonce légale) of company formation in an official legal gazette
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Legal gazette (e.g., Petites Affiches, Actions Légales)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff for legal announcements (tarif d'annonces légales)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code, principally Articles L.227-1 to L.227-20 and R.227-1 et seq. governing the Société par Actions Simplifiée; Articles L.123-1 et seq. governing commercial registration; Articles L.561-46 et seq. governing beneficial ownership disclosure; and Civil Code Articles 1832 et seq. governing companies.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The competent registry is the Registre National des Entreprises maintained by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle, with commercial registration processed through the Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises and reviewed by the competent Greffe du tribunal de commerce.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Electronic application for immatriculation of a société commerciale submitted through the Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises, together with the declaration of beneficial owners and supporting formation documents.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital applies to an SAS. The articles must state the share capital. At least 50% of cash contributions must be paid upon incorporation, with the balance payable within five years of registration. Contributions in kind must generally be fully paid at subscription. Funds may be deposited with a bank, notary, or Caisse des dépôts et consignations and released after registration. The amount excludes the beneficial-owner filing fee, legal-notice publication cost, professional fees, and possible additional registry charges.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The President records that the Company has been duly incorporated as a Société par Actions Simplifiée. It is resolved that the subscribers’ cash and in-kind contributions are accepted and the subscribed shares are issued in accordance with the articles and subscription schedule. The registered office is adopted at [full French address]. [Name] is appointed President for the term specified in the articles, and [name(s)] is/are appointed Director-General(s), if applicable. The President is authorized to open bank and payment accounts, complete all registry and beneficial-owner filings, and execute documents necessary to commence the Company’s restaurant operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm Corporate Particulars and Governance Structure
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founder and shareholder workstream; no government filing at this stage
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Determine the company name, purpose, registered office, duration, share capital, share classes, shareholder identities, President, optional Director-General, and decision rules. Verify the proposed name through the INPI database and confirm that the business purpose covers restaurant operations, food and condiment sales, delivery, and ancillary activities.
required_dossiers: Corporate shareholder certificate of incorporation and constitutional documents, if applicable
Registered-office title, lease, domiciliation agreement, or host certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct inconsistencies in names, addresses, powers, or corporate purpose before signature and filing. Obtain written shareholder approval for any revised governance provision.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute Articles and Subscribe the Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized bank, notary, or Caisse des dépôts et consignations for capital deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Sign the articles and subscription schedule. Deposit at least 50% of cash contributions into a blocked capital account and obtain the certificate of deposit. Document each contribution in kind; appoint a commissaire aux apports unless a statutory exemption is validly elected. Ensure signatures and powers of attorney are legally valid, with certified translations where required.
required_dossiers: Contribution-in-kind valuation report or valid exemption decision
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Replace incomplete bank documents, cure signature defects, or obtain a corrected contribution valuation report. Re-execute documents if the depositary rejects the file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized Journal of Legal Notices (Journal d'annonces légales) in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the legally required incorporation notice containing the company name, legal form, capital, registered office, duration, corporate purpose, President, and relevant transfer or approval provisions. Pay the applicable fixed publication tariff and obtain the certificate or attestation of publication.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request republication or a corrective notice if mandatory particulars are omitted or misstated. Retain both the original and corrective attestations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File for Registration and Beneficial-Owner Disclosure
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated through the INPI electronic portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create the electronic filing, upload the signed articles and supporting evidence, identify the principal activity and NAF code, submit beneficial-owner information, pay registry charges, and electronically sign the declaration. Use the French registered-office address and ensure the stated activity is consistent with the articles, lease, and tax registration.
required_dossiers: President declaration of non-conviction and parentage
Identification documents for officers and shareholders
Power of attorney, if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond electronically to a registry query within the stated deadline, upload corrected or missing documents, and pay any additional fee. If rejected, correct the filing and resubmit; challenge a legally unfounded refusal before the competent commercial court where appropriate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Registration Evidence and Activate Tax and Social Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique, SIRENE system operated by INSEE, and the competent Service des impôts des entreprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Download the registration extract and confirm the SIREN, SIRET, APE code, VAT status, and registered address. Open the operating bank account, transfer the deposited capital, register payroll and employer obligations where personnel will be hired, and establish accounting and VAT reporting procedures.
required_dossiers: Registration extract or current registration certificate
VAT and corporate-tax options, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request correction through the Guichet unique, INSEE, or the tax office if the legal name, activity, address, VAT status, or APE code is inaccurate. Maintain evidence of all correction requests.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Direction départementale de la protection des populations for food-establishment matters; competent mairie for alcohol-service declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before opening, submit the required declaration for an establishment handling food of animal origin where applicable, implement HACCP-based procedures, designate trained food-safety personnel, and maintain supplier, traceability, temperature, cleaning, and allergen records. File the applicable alcohol licence declaration at least 15 days before opening if alcohol is served.
required_dossiers: Alcohol licence declaration and licence documentation, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to DDPP or mairie requests, correct hygiene or licence deficiencies, and do not commence the affected activity until the required declaration or licence condition is satisfied.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Clear Premises, Fire Safety, Accessibility, and Employment Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Mairie and ERP safety/accessibility authorities; inspection bodies accredited for technical checks; competent labour authorities where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Classify the premises as an établissement recevant du public, obtain required building or fit-out authorizations, complete fire and accessibility checks, verify gas, electrical, ventilation, extraction, and structural installations, and prepare the workplace risk assessment. Maintain the DUERP, occupational-health arrangements, emergency procedures, and mandatory workplace notices.
required_dossiers: Electrical, gas, ventilation, and extraction inspection reports
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Remedy findings identified by the mairie, safety commission, inspection body, or labour inspectorate; obtain reinspection or written clearance before public opening where required.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No general industrial manufacturing board is normally required for a hotpot restaurant. The principal authorities are the Direction départementale de la protection des populations for food safety, the mairie for premises, ERP, and alcohol formalities, and the local sanitation authority for wastewater discharge. A project-specific Inspection des installations classées may apply if the premises fall within an ICPE classification.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Declaration of a food establishment handling foodstuffs of animal origin, where applicable, together with the applicable restaurant or alcohol-service licence. A restaurant serving alcohol must hold the relevant licence restaurant or licence III/IV and complete the required mairie declaration.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for Ecological Transition, through the competent regional environmental authority, the Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Ordinarily exempt from a standalone environmental impact assessment for a standard urban restaurant. Project-specific screening is required for major construction, sensitive sites, significant combustion or refrigeration installations, or an installation classified under the ICPE regime.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Discharge to the public sewer must comply with the local sanitation authority's authorization and applicable French water and wastewater rules; grease interceptors and appropriate pretreatment may be required for kitchen effluent. Separate and properly dispose of used cooking oil, bio-waste, packaging, and hazardous waste through authorized contractors. Control cooking fumes, odors, ventilation, and any VOC or combustion emissions under applicable building, occupational, municipal, or ICPE requirements. No universal restaurant-specific VOC threshold applies outside an applicable regulated installation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The premises must satisfy ERP fire-safety and accessibility requirements, including emergency exits, alarm and extinguishing equipment, evacuation signage, emergency lighting, and safe public occupancy. Gas, electrical, extraction, ventilation, and structural installations must be inspected as applicable. The operator must maintain the DUERP, provide occupational-health arrangements, conduct required worker training, implement hygiene and personal-protective procedures, and retain inspection and maintenance records.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des finances publiques (DGFiP), including the relevant Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE) and, for non-established foreign businesses, the Service des impôts des entreprises étrangères (SIEE); principal digital portals are impots.gouv.fr and the French business formalities portal formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SAS is incorporated through the single business formalities portal, which transmits registration information to the competent registries and tax authorities. The resulting SIREN identifies the legal entity and the SIRET identifies each establishment. The SAS must file its business creation and tax information with the competent SIE, including its activity, registered office, establishments, bank details, accounting period, and VAT position. The French VAT number is issued by the DGFiP and normally consists of the prefix FR, a two-character control key, and the nine-digit SIREN. A foreign entity without a French establishment that makes taxable transactions in France applies to the SIEE for a French VAT number using the applicable registration documentation, transaction evidence, identity and corporate documents, banking information, and proof of business activity. An EU-established business generally does not need a French fiscal representative; a non-EU-established business generally must appoint an accredited French fiscal representative unless an applicable mutual-assistance exemption applies. VAT registration must be completed before taxable activity requiring French VAT collection, and intra-EU operators must also obtain the applicable EU VAT identification status.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A French SAS is generally subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés) by default. A qualifying SAS may elect temporary income-tax treatment under Article 239 bis AB of the French Tax Code if statutory conditions are satisfied, including qualifying ownership, activity, turnover, employee, age, and non-listed-company requirements. The election is generally available for a maximum period of five fiscal years and must be notified within the statutory deadline. There is no general United States-style check-the-box election. French anti-hybrid mismatch rules implement the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive framework and can deny deductions or impose inclusion consequences; they do not provide a general elective hybrid classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT), with customs and import VAT rules for goods entering France or the European Union.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For a French-established business using the franchise en base de TVA, the principal annual turnover threshold for services, including restaurant services, is EUR 37,500, subject to the applicable tolerance threshold of EUR 41,250 under current rules. A business exceeding the relevant threshold loses the exemption under the statutory timing rules. A SAS conducting taxable restaurant operations may nevertheless elect or be required to operate under the normal VAT regime, and VAT registration can be required from the first taxable transaction where the franchise regime is unavailable or not applicable. Reduced VAT rates may apply to qualifying food and non-alcoholic beverage sales, while restaurant services and alcoholic beverages generally require transaction-level classification rather than automatic application of the 20% rate.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France does not currently operate a universal real-time invoice-clearance system for all domestic transactions. Mandatory B2B e-invoicing is being phased in: all French-established businesses must be able to receive compliant electronic invoices from 1 September 2026; issuance obligations apply to large and intermediate-sized enterprises from 1 September 2026 and to small and medium-sized enterprises and micro-enterprises from 1 September 2027, subject to legislative and regulatory implementation details. E-invoices must be transmitted through an approved private platform, with structured data reported to the French tax administration. B2C and certain cross-border transaction data are subject to e-reporting requirements. Public-sector invoices are submitted through the Chorus Pro system. Businesses must maintain compliant point-of-sale records, VAT invoices, credit notes, audit trails, and accounting data; there is no general requirement for digital fiscal stamping or prior DGFiP clearance of ordinary restaurant invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods dispatched from France to a destination outside the European Union may qualify for VAT exemption with the right to deduct, provided the supplier establishes that the goods physically left the EU customs territory and that the export was made by or on behalf of the supplier or the customer in accordance with French VAT rules. Intra-EU supplies may qualify for exemption where the customer has a valid VAT number in another Member State and the goods are transported to that Member State, supported by the required transport and reporting evidence. Services supplied to a foreign business may be outside the scope of French VAT under place-of-supply rules, but this is not generally a zero-rated export. Restaurant and catering services are normally taxable where physically performed; an overseas brand or customer location does not by itself create export treatment. Export refunds and input VAT recovery require valid invoices, customs evidence, transport evidence, accounting records, and consistency between VAT returns, customs declarations, and commercial documentation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: French or EU customs export declaration containing the Movement Reference Number (MRN)
Electronic confirmation of exit from the EU customs territory or equivalent customs exit certification
Commercial invoice identifying the exporter, customer, goods, values, delivery terms, and destination
Packing list and product identification records
Transport evidence, such as bill of lading, air waybill, CMR consignment note, or courier proof of delivery
Evidence linking the goods, invoice, customs declaration, and transport record
Import or destination-country customs evidence where necessary to corroborate arrival
VAT return and accounting records supporting the exemption and input VAT deduction
Intra-EU VAT identification and transport evidence where the transaction is an exempt intra-Community supply
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France has no general foreign-exchange control rule requiring export proceeds to be repatriated within 180 days. Export receipts may therefore be held or received through ordinary commercial banking arrangements, subject to anti-money-laundering, sanctions, accounting, and payment-service requirements. If export exemption is unsupported, the DGFiP may reassess output VAT, deny related input VAT recovery, charge late-payment interest generally calculated at 0.20% per month, and impose penalties generally ranging from 10% for specified filing or payment failures to 40% for deliberate conduct and up to 80% for fraudulent manoeuvres or abuse of rights. Serious tax fraud may also trigger criminal sanctions, including imprisonment and substantial fines, with higher limits in aggravated cases. Customs declarations may be corrected and customs debt, import VAT, customs penalties, and other administrative sanctions may be imposed under the Union Customs Code and French law. Refunds obtained through false export evidence may be clawed back, with penalties assessed retrospectively.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France maintains full capital account convertibility under EU law and IMF Article VIII obligations. Current account transactions, including profit remittances to non-resident shareholders, face no convertibility restrictions. Large-value transactions exceeding €100,000 require statistical reporting to the Banque de France. Profit remittance hurdles are minimal provided beneficial ownership documentation and source-of-funds verification are maintained.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds are not subject to mandatory surrender in France. Companies must file export declarations via the Foreign Trade Single Window (BDF) using the Single Administrative Document (SAD) within statutory timelines. No statutory conversion ratios or surrender obligations apply; proceeds may be retained in foreign-currency accounts. Statistical reporting to the Banque de France is mandatory within 30 days of export.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Fintech electronic money institutions (EMIs) such as PayPal, Wise, or Stripe offer high feasibility for cross-border receipts and disbursements for French SAS entities. Legal constraints include mandatory compliance with French AML/KYC standards, potential requirement for local banking facilitation, and restrictions on offshore wallet custody without proper regulatory approvals.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote digital onboarding and KYC are permitted for French SAS under Banque de France and ACPR guidelines. Physical presence and in-person KYC interviews are required only for high-risk profiles, complex ownership structures, or when requested by the bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Undisclosed beneficial ownership or shell-company indicators
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Ultimate beneficial owner declarations, corporate structure charts, and proof of economic substance

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transactions linked to high-risk jurisdictions or unexplained fund sources
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Enhanced due diligence reports, source-of-wealth statements, and regulatory approvals

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections are processed via SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 'CAP' or 'EQTY'. Verification requires board resolutions, shareholder agreements, tax identification numbers, and beneficial ownership certificates. All flows must comply with French AML regulations and reporting thresholds.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements utilize SWIFT MT103 for international payments and Commercial Letters of Credit under UCP 600 for trade settlements. Purpose codes include 'PAY' for general payments and 'TRAD' for trade-related disbursements. Commercial LCs require presentation of compliant shipping documents.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual accounts and allocation of profit or loss
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: SAS shareholders; no routine filing authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the financial year-end, unless a court-approved extension applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Potential shareholder or creditor liability; failure to approve accounts may support court proceedings and administrative enforcement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of annual accounts and applicable management report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Court Registry (Greffe du tribunal de commerce) through the INPI one-stop-shop portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval of the accounts, or within two months if filed electronically
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court injunction may be issued; civil fine may reach approximately EUR 1,500, increasing for repeat non-compliance. Persistent default may result in registry enforcement, but there is no automatic annual strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return Form 2065 and financial schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after financial year-end; for a 31 December year-end, generally by the second business day after 1 May
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest generally at 0.20% per month and a 10% surcharge for late filing or payment, subject to applicable exceptions and adjustments.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT return under the simplified VAT regime, if applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Form CA12 generally due by the second business day after 1 May following the relevant calendar year; not applicable where the normal VAT regime applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing and late-payment surcharges, generally including 0.20% monthly interest and a 10% surcharge, subject to statutory relief.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Cotisation Foncière des Entreprises (CFE) annual tax payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally payable by 15 December each year through the business tax account
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest and surcharges may apply; non-payment can trigger enforced collection procedures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual review of beneficial ownership, shareholding, directors, registered office, and corporate registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate records; updates filed with the INPI one-stop-shop portal where required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Review at least annually; changes to beneficial ownership or registered particulars should generally be reported within 30 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to declare or update beneficial ownership information may result in injunctions, fines, and restrictions on filing or registration; no separate annual confirmation fee applies.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor is generally mandatory when the SAS exceeds at least two of three thresholds: EUR 5 million balance-sheet total, EUR 10 million net turnover, and 50 average employees. Additional group-based appointment rules may apply to parent, subsidiary, or controlled companies.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French Generally Accepted Accounting Principles under the French Accounting Standards Authority (ANC) General Accounting Plan. IFRS applies primarily to qualifying consolidated accounts or where legally permitted and adopted.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not require a standalone annual beneficial-owner confirmation. The SAS should perform an annual verification of ownership and control, record the review, and file any change in beneficial ownership or related particulars through the INPI portal generally within 30 days.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members or shareholder ownership records
Register of Directors and corporate officers
Minute Book of shareholder and corporate decisions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 350-1,500 annually for commercial domiciliation; France generally does not require a separate registered agent.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 2,500-8,000 annually for a small SAS, depending on turnover, locations, inventory, payroll, group reporting, and audit complexity.

stage_6.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax holidays or preferential deductions
